liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Help on the Way** (3 reviews): Second-set Help>Slipknot>Franklin's Tower served as the springboard for the set's best playing; Help includes excursions into electronic sound art [22][26][31]
- **Jack Straw** (3 reviews): Jack Straw has an amazing crescendo just before the last verse; a favorite of the reviewer; Second-set Help>Slip>Franklin's>Jack Straw run is called smokin' [29][30][31]
- **He's Gone** (3 reviews): He's Gone is described as going ballistic; Seamless vocal jam from He's Gone into Smokestack, with the audience catching on at the first hint [25][26][27]
- **Smokestack Lightnin'** (2 reviews): First full Smokestack in a while; band only teased it at Hampton without lyrics, and crowd erupted when Bobby sang; Smokestack called the first in ages; crowd goes wild and Jerry riffs hard [23][33]
- **Dancin' in the Streets** (1 review): The band gets deeply into the jam in Dancin' [30]
- **Stella Blue** (1 review): Reviewer calls this the best Stella Blue; the band lets the jam drift away at the end [26]

## Setlist highlights

- **Percussion space**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 4 archived performances [34]
- **Revolution**: rare: 12 archived performances [34]

## The recordings

- **gd1984-10-09.nak300.carpenter.wise.andrewf.81386.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): source not stated; 23 songs; 154 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]. Said about its sound: Tape-deck malfunction left a high-pitched whine, attenuated with EQ but audible on headphones near Big Railroad [1]
- **gd1984-10-09.110019.beyer-senn-daweez.D5scott.flac16**: source not stated; 23 songs; 148 min [2]
- **gd84-10-09.sbd.wiley.14499.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 22 songs; 165 min; rated 4.27/5 by 22 [5]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds the recording perfect; Audience is close, tapers sound inspired, and the sound is sparkling [27][31]
- **gd1984-10-09.168001.beyer.m160.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 22 songs; 154 min [7]
- **gd1984-10-09.senn421.pauline.miller.91410.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 22 songs; 151 min; rated 4.2/5 by 5 [12]. Said about its sound: Reviewer calls this the best-sounding source available [33]
- **gd1984-10-09.beyerm88.suraci.77880.flac16**: source not stated; 22 songs; 146 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [13]

## Around the show

- Show fell on John Lennon's birthday, when the band reportedly always played well [25]
- Small, cozy venue with intimate feel and heavy party scene during fall 1984 tour [27]
- Area around the Centrum in Worcester was rough and inner-city, but inside the venue that was forgotten [30]
- Whooshing sound in the second half of Revolution comes from the PA, not the tape [1]
- Reviewer judges this the better of the two Centrum nights [22]
- Back end of the show is weaker than the first set [23]
- Reviewer considers 1984 and this show underrated [33]
- Recording is not as close as the first night's tape, but still front-of-board [13]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1984-10-09.nak300.carpenter.wise.andrewf.81386.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Ted Carpenter; transferred by Jim Wise and Andrew F.; source: FOB, Nakamichi CM-300's with CP-4 shotgun capsules > Sony TC-D5M > Maxell UD-XLII's, no Dolby [1]. Also: Tape flips at Let it Grow start and in Drums were patched or cross-faded; He's Gone dropout patched from another source [1]
- **gd1984-10-09.110019.beyer-senn-daweez.D5scott.flac16**: taped by Da Weez; transferred by D5scott; source: source: 2 Beyer M160 & 1 Sennheiser 421 microphones > Nak MX100 w/2001 > Sony TC-D5M (Dolby on) - analog master cassettes; [2]. Also: Recorded with Beyer, Senn and Daweez mics; dedicated to friend Sandy 'Bigfoot', who was not involved in the taping [2]
- **gd84-10-09.sbd.wiley.14499.sbeok.shnf**: source: MAC>>Sony D-5>CDR>SHN (previous upgraded SHN release) ; Via Andy L. ; Seeded to Etree by T. Wiley [5]. Also: Source is a crisp soundboard with patches from a MAC>Sony lineage, contrary to the listed description [28]
- **gd1984-10-09.168001.beyer.m160.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Jim Vita; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Jim Vita's Master (FOB) Audience Cassettes; Beyer M160 mics > Sony D5M (Maxell XLII-S) [7]
- **gd1984-10-09.senn421.pauline.miller.91410.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Rick Pauline; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Sennheiser 421 -> Cassette Master (Sony D5/Maxell XLII-S90) D [12]
- **gd1984-10-09.beyerm88.suraci.77880.flac16**: taped by Tony Suraci; transferred by Tony Suraci; source: FOB/Beyer M88>Sony D5 [13]. Also: Taped with Beyer M88 microphones; this is the 16-bit version, with 24-bit on DVDA [13]

claims.text: Second-set Help>Slipknot>Franklin's Tower served as the springboard for the set's best playing
Reviewer judges this the better of the two Centrum nights
First full Smokestack in a while; band only teased it at Hampton without lyrics, and crowd erupted when Bobby sang
Back end of the show is weaker than the first set
He's Gone is described as going ballistic
Show fell on John Lennon's birthday, when the band reportedly always played well
Help includes excursions into electronic sound art
Seamless vocal jam from He's Gone into Smokestack, with the audience catching on at the first hint
Reviewer calls this the best Stella Blue; the band lets the jam drift away at the end
Small, cozy venue with intimate feel and heavy party scene during fall 1984 tour
Jerry sounds trippy and excellent on He's Gone into Smokestack
Reviewer finds the recording perfect
Source is a crisp soundboard with patches from a MAC>Sony lineage, contrary to the listed description
Jack Straw has an amazing crescendo just before the last verse; a favorite of the reviewer
Area around the Centrum in Worcester was rough and inner-city, but inside the venue that was forgotten
The band gets deeply into the jam in Dancin'
Second-set Help>Slip>Franklin's>Jack Straw run is called smokin'
Worcester Jack Straw topped the reviewer's annual group vote for best Jack Straw
Audience is close, tapers sound inspired, and the sound is sparkling
Help>Slip>Franklin's has Phil booming and lifting the night into another gear
Reviewer calls this the best-sounding source available
Smokestack called the first in ages; crowd goes wild and Jerry riffs hard
Reviewer considers 1984 and this show underrated
Tape flips at Let it Grow start and in Drums were patched or cross-faded; He's Gone dropout patched from another source
Tape-deck malfunction left a high-pitched whine, attenuated with EQ but audible on headphones near Big Railroad
Whooshing sound in the second half of Revolution comes from the PA, not the tape
Recorded with Beyer, Senn and Daweez mics; dedicated to friend Sandy 'Bigfoot', who was not involved in the taping
Transferred by Charlie Miller from Jim Vita's master cassettes; Sennheiser 421 source supplies a 6:26 patch in Drums
Taped with Beyer M88 microphones; this is the 16-bit version, with 24-bit on DVDA
Recording is not as close as the first night's tape, but still front-of-board
